title: Same Car. Theo's "Cheap" Loan Cost $5,326 More 🚗
description:
Same $45,000 car, same 7% rate. Nora took a 4-year loan at $1,078/month. Theo picked 7 years because $679/month felt cheaper. By year 4 Nora's car is paid off and Theo still owes about $22,000 — and over the full loan he pays $12,050 in interest vs her $6,724. That's $5,326 extra for the "cheap" payment.

A lower monthly payment isn't the same as a cheaper car — check the total interest before you sign.

Would you take 4 years or 7? 👇

Follow for more numbers that change how you spend.

⚠️ Assumptions: $45,000 financed at 7% APR on both loans (Edmunds Q3 2026 average new-car APR: 7%; 25.5% of financed new cars used loans of 84+ months), fixed monthly payments, no fees, taxes or insurance. Longer loans often come with higher rates, so the real gap can be bigger. Nora and Theo are fictional. Numbers are an illustration only. This is not financial advice.
